inspiration.observed_pattern: A self-join pairs each row with the immediately preceding calendar date using DATE_ADD, then filters for a strictly larger measurement.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independent sensor-temperature audit. Readings are joined within each station on exact one-day adjacency, only rises are returned, missing dates do not pair, and deterministic station/date ordering makes the result stable; the source schema, names, and values are not copied.

fixture_notes: Station 10 rises from 40 to 45 on July 2 but falls on July 3 and has a July 5 gap; station 20 rises from 79 to 81 on July 3; station 30 has only one reading. Only exact consecutive-day rises should be returned.
determinism_notes: Station IDs, reading dates, temperatures, exact one-day interval, comparison, and final ordering are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE sensor_readings (reading_id INT PRIMARY KEY, station_id INT NOT NULL, reading_on DATE NOT NULL, temperature_c DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT current_reading.reading_id, current_reading.station_id, current_reading.reading_on, current_reading.temperature_c, prior_reading.temperature_c AS prior_temperature_c FROM sensor_readings AS current_reading INNER JOIN sensor_readings AS prior_reading ON current_reading.station_id = prior_reading.station_id AND current_reading.reading_on = DATE_ADD(prior_reading.reading_on, INTERVAL 1 DAY) WHERE current_reading.temperature_c > prior_reading.temperature_c ORDER BY current_reading.station_id, current_reading.reading_on

checks.sql: SELECT reading_id, station_id, reading_on, temperature_c FROM sensor_readings ORDER BY reading_id
